text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

WHEAT SALES - Tunisia purchased six lots of 25,000 tonnes each of U.S. origin wheat at between $148.21 and $159.95 per tonne C&F for August to October shipment, buyers told Reuters. The deal included half No. 2 hard red winter wheat from $159.44 to $159.95 and half soft red winter from $148.21 to $151.05.

WHEAT SALES - The Taiwan Flour Mills Association bought 66,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat Friday, traders said. For July 15-30 shipment it bought 21,900 tonnes of dark northern spring (DNS) at $189.89, 9,100 of HRW at $174.49 and 2,000 of white wheat at $156.36. For August 5-20 shipment it bought 19,800 of DNS at $188.77, 9,000 of HRW at $177.48 and 4,200 white at $152.35
- The Commodity Credit Corp (CCC) bought 44,731 tonnes of hard red winter wheat for donation to Ethiopia, the CCC said. It paid $141.43 per tonne, FOB, to Cargill Inc. Shipment is for July 15-30.

CORN SALE - The Korea Feed Association's members in Pusan bought 52,000 tonnes of corn at $125.30 a tonne C&F late Thursday from Cargill Inc, traders said. Arrival was for October 15 to Pusan. Shipment was for August 22-September 10 if from the U.S. Gulf and for September 11-30 if from the Pacific Northwest. The seller can also deliver Chinese corn at $121.30 a tonne, C&F, they said.
WHEAT TENDERS - The CCC seeks July 1 60,000 tonnes of US HRW wheat for July 16-31 shipment for donation to Kyrgyzstan.
SOYMEAL TENDER - The CCC was scheduled to tender July 2 for 4,560 tonnes of U.S. soymeal for donation to Guatemala. Shipment is for July 17-31.

MARKET TALK - Brazil exported 1.80 million tonnes of soybeans in May, up 49.4 percent from April, inspection company SGS do Brasil said. Exports of soymeal were stable at 1.20 million tonnes while soyoil exports increased 53.1 percent month-on-month to 181,900 tonnes, SGS said. There were no comparisons with 1996.

MARKET TALK - U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said Friday he would like to see funding for the Export Enhancement Program restored in the House spending bill, but was sympathetic to budget constraints faced by lawmakers. Earlier this week, the House Appropriations subcommittee on agriculture approved a fiscal 1998 spending plan that limits funding for the subsidy program to $270 million, well below the Clinton Administration's request for $500 million.
MARKET TALK - U.S. Agriculture Department Friday said it added Tanzania to the East Africa Region countries eligible for the Export Credit Guarantee Program (GSM-102) for fiscal year 1997.
